children: Infosys Limited Sponsored ADR (NSE:INFY) says a temporary U.S. PERM filing suspension won’t materially hit staffing as it leans on AI-driven offshore delivery, ramps hiring and AI services (now >8% revenue) that analysts expect to drive modest margin and revenue gains ahead of Oct 23 results.
Previous Week Recap
PERM Filing Suspension Impact
: U.S. Labor Department suspended new and pending PERM filings for Infosys ADR (INFY). Filing and processing halted; existing H‑1B visas remain valid. Infosys says no material U.S. impact.
INFY Q2 FY27 Revenue Outlook
: Analysts predict Infosys ADR (INFY) Q2 FY27 revenue ₹49,090–₹49,323 crore (seq. +1.7%–2.3%; cc +1.1%–1.7%) and PAT ₹8,026–₹8,100 crore.
AI Tools Use, Hiring
: Infosys (INFY): ~80,000 employees use AI coding tools, AI services made over 8% of revenue last quarter and grew double digits sequentially; company plans to hire 20,000 graduates this FY.
AI Could Be 20–30%
: Infosys CEO Salil Parekh says AI services could make up 20%–30% of work in a few quarters and near 50% of work within two to three years.
PERM Suspension No Material
: INFY said PERM filings were single digits over two years and that PERM processing suspension won’t materially affect its workforce strategy or client projects.
Project Maximus Margin Benefit
: PL Capital expects Infosys ADR (INFY) to see ~40 bps sequential EBIT margin gain from Project Maximus and FX tailwinds, partly offset by amortization and AI investments.
Board Meeting, Results Timeline
: Infosys ADR (INFY) will hold a board meeting Oct 22–23, 2026. Quarterly results for period ended Sept 30, 2026 are expected Oct 23, 2026; dividend approval may be considered.
U.S. Hiring, Offshore Delivery

: Infosys ADR (INFY) may boost U.S. hiring, expand regional delivery centers, and use more remote workshops and offshore delivery as AI shifts economics and visa limits affect onshore/offshore staffing
Q2 Manpower Data Omission
: Infosys ADR (INFY) was omitted from industry Q2 headcount data because it hadn’t provided Q2 manpower figures ahead of its October 23 earnings release.
Rising AI-Driven Demand
: Infosys (INFY) sees rising demand for AI-driven IT services as enterprises pursue complex transformations. Co-founder Nandan Nilekani dismissed AI job-loss claims, calling such warnings alarmist.
